The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 641d4aa3892adbca), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 55. statement: Fix base data satisfying (7.1). Fix b∗, δ0, δ, ao > 0 and L ≥ 1. For every sufficiently large finite M, C2 can be chosen depending on these parameters, and then ε > 0 can be chosen arbitrarily small and D1, D2 sufficiently large but finite, so that (7.3)–(7.4) at u∗ = 1 has a positive solution on the full attached exterior. It is smooth on each closed side of C and tends to the specified values at infinity. It satisfies 0 ≤ f ≤ M, Ni, No ≤ C(L)M, ∫︂ Ωi W2 ≤ C(L)M2 , Ni ≥ cε, si, No ≥ c(M, L)ε. (7.9) The constants in these bounds do not depend on ε, D1, D2 or the outer truncation. Dependence on the fixed data and on the preceding parameters is suppressed. At fixed M, L, ε, the lapse and height have uniform local continuity bounds off the seam, including at S, independent of D1, D2. Moreover w ≥ M9/10 where f ≥ 9M/10, x ≥ 1 on DM ∩ {N ≤ 2ε}, (7.10) and ∫︂ P1 ≤ C(L)M−1/10 , ∫︂ P2 ≤ ωM (ε), ωM (ε) −→ 0 (ε ↓ 0). (7.11) The function ωM is uniform in the finite strengths and outer radius. In particular ∫︂ DM ∩{x<1−δ} W ≤ C/L, (7.12) where C is independent of L, M, ε, D1, D2. On the smooth sides the metric h = xḡ obeys the scalar and boundary identities (7.22) and (7.23) below. Its asymptotically flat mass satisfies mh ≤ mo + C(b∗ + δ0) + C(L)M−1/10 + CωM (ε). (7.13) Thus the parameter order is: fix the base data; choose b∗, δ0 for the mass tolerance; choose δ, ao and then L for the area tolerance; choose M large; choose C2; choose ε small; choose the finite strengths; and finally let the outer radius tend to infinity.
